item.title: EuroSTEMPeers 2026 — Talk: "EU AI Act – Everything You Need to Know"
item.description:
A short talk on the EU AI Act aimed at researchers and early-career scientists navigating what the regulation actually requires of them — cutting through the legal language to explain the practical compliance questions that come up when adopting AI tools in a research setting.

Drawing on her specialist knowledge of the EU AI Act and EU Digital Act, and having worked on AI products since 2019, Pranoti focused on what’s genuinely relevant for a working scientist rather than a full legal breakdown: which AI use cases carry which obligations, and how to evaluate tools for compliance before adopting them in a lab or research group.

item.title: EuroSTEMPeers 2026 — Workshop: "Grant Preparation & CV Customisation"
item.description:
A hands-on workshop on using generative AI tools to strengthen grant applications and tailor CVs to specific funding calls — practical workflows rather than theory, drawn from Pranoti’s work helping researchers submit European proposals worth more than €32 million.

The session focused on where AI genuinely speeds up proposal writing (structuring arguments, tightening language, adapting a CV to a specific call’s priorities) versus where it can introduce risk if used carelessly, giving attendees a workflow they could take straight into their next grant application.

item.title: HdM Quantum Day
item.description: At HdM Quantum Day 2026, Pranoti spoke about the strategic partnership between QuanTour and The Science Talk, and how partnerships like this can amplify research impact. As communication lead for the QuanTour project — winner of the 2025 Lise Meitner Medal and Prize from the Institute of Physics for innovative public engagement across the UK and Europe — she brought a practitioner’s view of what makes science communication partnerships actually work.

item.title: Neurodiversity in the Earth and Environmental Sciences: Awareness to Action
item.description:
A panel discussion at the NWO NAC 2026 conference, addressing neurodiversity awareness and advocacy within the Earth and Environmental Sciences community — sharing personal experience alongside two other panelists and a moderator, in front of an audience of Masters students through professors.

“Pranoti is very open and engaging, which made for an amazing discussion about neurodiversity in academia. And I think she did a great job expressing a lot of the challenges neurodiverse people face in academia as well as in corporations. Just really nice to work with all around.”

item.description:
At the YES Meeting 2023 in Landau, Pranoti delivered both a Personal Branding Workshop and a Science Communication Training session for early-career environmental scientists.

“I found the workshop insightful and inspiring to further develop my own personal brand as a scientist on professional social media. Dr Kshirsagar graciously shared her own tips and tricks to enhance visibility, increase engagement and grow followers. I would recommend the workshop if you are looking for structure of ways to ‘shine’ in the digital world!”
